An elegant two-handed sword. Normal attacks fill a Spirit Gauge; named Spirit techniques replace one of your attacks from the Attack action and spend that gauge. Each technique works on its own — with Extra Attack you can chain two in the same action if you pay both costs.

Open Longsword filters on 5e.tools

Features

Mastery (Sap)

If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Spirit Gauge

This weapon holds up to 6 spirit (the gauge starts empty). When you hit a creature with a normal attack using this weapon (an attack you did not replace with a Spirit technique), you gain 1 spirit. You lose all spirit if you don't hit a creature with this weapon within 1 minute or if you become Incapacitated.

Spirit techniques that replace an attack do not generate spirit. You cannot apply Spirit Blade to the same attack you replace with a Spirit technique.

Spirit Blade

When you hit with a normal attack using this weapon, you can expend any number of spirits: the attack deals an extra [[/r 1d4]] slashing damage per spirit expended. You cannot use Spirit Blade on an attack you replaced with Spirit Thrust, Spirit Roundslash, or Spirit Helm Breaker.

▸ Upgrade — Spirit Blade Upgrade I

Spirit Blade extra damage increases to [[/r 1d6]] slashing per spirit expended.

Foresight Slash

Reaction.

As a Reaction when a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack, you can expend 2 spirits. Roll [[/r 1d8]] and add it to your AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. If this causes the attack to miss, you can make one attack with this weapon against the attacker as part of the same Reaction, and you regain 1 spirit. You can't use this feature if you have no spirit.
